symptom: Windows, JRE 21 and JDK 21 installed side by side, JAVA_HOME unset: `mxcli test --local` / `run --local` built with the JRE and MxBuild failed with "Java compiler is not available. Please check that …\\jre-21.0.5.11-hotspot contains a valid JDK installation".
cause: resolveJDK's isJDK only checked that bin/java ran and reported the right major. The Windows search globs match jdk-* only, but the PATH step came first, and the Adoptium JRE installer puts its bin on PATH; a JRE reports the same `java -version`.
file: cmd/mxcli/docker/detect.go (isJDK -> jdkAt, hasJavaCompiler, javaTool; JAVA_HOME message)
fix: A JDK must have bin/javac (or javac.exe) as well as a java of the requested major; JAVA_HOME, PATH and the search globs all go through it. The not-found error names a JAVA_HOME that is a JRE.
insight: A version check is not a capability check: what MxBuild needs from a JDK is the compiler, so test for the compiler. The candidate order (JAVA_HOME, macOS java_home, PATH, globs) means any earlier step can hand over a JRE that the globs would never match — fix the predicate all steps share, not one step. Testable from Linux by checking both javac and javac.exe and injecting `java -version`.
test: cmd/mxcli/docker/detect_jre_2186_test.go (JRE on PATH + JDK in the Adoptium folder, both exe spellings; JAVA_HOME on a JRE is named; control: wrong major refused); with the compiler check stubbed the JRE is chosen
